contract_change.repair: The projection revision (GraphDisplay.source_revision Counter) is row content identity per DC-MP-FLOW1 (a row is reused only when both the projection revision and the full GraphRef match). same_match_content now requires full revision equality, the shell clears the cache on every revision change again, and a projection-counter-only change rebuilds. Publication-version-only reuse is retained because the admitted rows are pinned by the exact projection revision and canonical GraphRef.

budget.measured_interval: match-set obtain + diagram construction only (publication reuse or projection rebuild). Rows re-derivation and layers are excluded; the timer is not a frame timer.
budget.frame_wide_note: No frame-wide compliance is claimed. The same session's ten_thousand_node_flow_phases_stay_within_the_frame_budget test reports frame_within_ui_p95=false (frame path median 15,064 / p95 21,400 us) and the revision-change series display_total p95 is 27,262 us (query-only) and 37,390 us (revision). For the publication-version-only path, layers stay cached (revision key unchanged) and rows run in the background, so the display composition is match reuse + diagram; that composition was not measured together with paint.

known_limits: The reuse predicate treats the exact projection revision counters and the canonical GraphRef sequence, plus the query and session/epoch scope, as the content identity (DC-MP-FLOW1: a row is reused only when both the projection revision and the full GraphRef match). Only the publication version may differ for a reuse.
The cache remains single-entry, shell-owned and bounded; there is no global state.
The measurements time CPU path generation only; they are not window frame times.
